Full job description
We are seeking an experienced and organized Project Manager to lead projects from initiation through completion. The Project Manager will be responsible for planning, coordinating, and managing project resources, schedules, budgets, and risks while ensuring successful delivery that meets business objectives and stakeholder expectations.

Key Responsibilities
Define project scope, objectives, deliverables, and success criteria.
Develop and maintain detailed project plans, schedules, and budgets.
Coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure project milestones are achieved.
Monitor project progress and proactively address risks, issues, and changes.
Manage stakeholder expectations through regular communication and status reporting.
Ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and according to quality standards.
Allocate resources effectively and optimize team performance.
Facilitate project meetings, workshops, and decision-making sessions.
Track project performance using key performance indicators (KPIs).
Maintain project documentation, including plans, reports, and lessons learned.
Ensure compliance with organizational policies, industry standards, and contractual requirements.
Support continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to enhance project management processes.

Requirements

Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
3–7+ years of project management experience.
Strong knowledge of project management methodologies (Waterfall, Agile, or Hybrid).
Proficiency with project management tools such as Microsoft Project, Jira, Asana, Trello, or Monday.com.
Excellent leadership, communication, negotiation, and organizational skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Preferred Qualifications
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
PRINCE2, Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP), or Scrum Master certification.
Experience managing cross-functional and geographically distributed teams.

Benefits
Private Health Insurance
Training & Development
Performance Bonus

Permanent

Full job description
Department: Group Management
Reports To: Chief Executive Officer
Location: UAE / Regional
Employment Type: Full-Time
Job Level: Senior Management
Scope: Group-wide – UAE, KSA and future international markets
Role Summary:

The Group Technology Transformation Lead is ultimately responsible for connecting business strategy, commercial requirements, operations and technology.

The Group is therefore seeking more than an ERP project manager or IT specialist. The successful candidate must be capable of understanding the business in depth, advising senior management on technology decisions, challenging vendors and implementation partners, and personally leading a complex multi-year transformation from strategy through successful implementation and adoption.

1. Role Purpose

The Group Technology Transformation Lead is responsible for defining, leading and delivering the Group's technology strategy and transformation roadmap across its businesses and international operations.

The role combines technology leadership, business partnership and transformation delivery. The successful candidate will work closely with the CEO and management team to understand the Group's commercial objectives, operational requirements and growth plans, and translate these into scalable technology solutions.

In the short term, the role will take ownership of the current technology landscape, systems, vendors, costs, integrations and immediate business requirements, while establishing stronger technology governance and supporting current technology decisions.

In the long term, the role will design and lead a long term Group-wide technology transformation covering ERP, CRM, contact centre, HR, booking/POS, inventory, e-commerce, data, integrations, automation and reporting.

This is not a traditional IT support or general project-management position. The role requires a senior, hands-on technology transformation professional with recent experience delivering complex enterprise systems implementations and the commercial and operational understanding required to make effective technology decisions for the business.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. Technology Strategy & Business Partnership

Act as the principal technology business partner to the CEO and management team.
Develop a detailed understanding of the Group's businesses, commercial models, operations, customers and growth strategy.
Work closely with Finance, HR, Operations, Marketing, Sales, Contact Centre and other functions to understand business requirements and priorities.
Translate commercial and operational requirements into technology strategy and solutions.
Identify opportunities where technology can improve revenue, conversion, productivity, customer experience, controls and scalability.
Evaluate technology decisions based on business value, cost, ROI, risk and scalability.
Provide clear recommendations to management, including alternatives, costs, risks and implementation implications.
Ensure technology supports business processes and strategy rather than unnecessarily dictating them.
Maintain awareness of emerging technologies, automation and AI opportunities relevant to the Group.
B. Current Technology Environment & Short-Term Management

Conduct a comprehensive review of the existing technology landscape across the Group.
Maintain visibility over all systems, platforms, licences, subscriptions, integrations, vendors and technology-related contracts.
Review current technology expenditure, utilisation and contractual commitments.
Identify system duplication, gaps, inefficiencies, risks and manual workarounds.
Establish clear system and business ownership.
Take ownership of key technology vendor relationships and escalations.
Support management with immediate system and technology decisions.
Introduce appropriate governance for technology purchasing, system changes and vendor engagement.
Identify and implement appropriate short-term improvements without compromising the future technology architecture.
Ensure current business operations remain adequately supported throughout the transformation period.
C. Group Technology Architecture & Transformation Roadmap

Define the Group's current-state and target-state technology architecture.
Develop and maintain a structured 2–3 year technology transformation roadmap.
Determine which systems and capabilities should operate at Group, business and country level.
Establish implementation priorities, sequencing, dependencies and budgets.
Ensure proposed architecture supports multi-company, multi-country and future international expansion.
Establish technology standards and principles covering systems, integrations, data, security and governance.
Develop business cases for significant technology investments.
Present technology recommendations and investment requirements to the CEO and management team.
D. ERP Transformation

Lead the evaluation, selection and implementation of the Group's future ERP environment, with NetSuite currently under consideration.

Responsibilities include:

Business requirements gathering.
Current-state and future-state process mapping.
Fit-gap analysis.
ERP evaluation and selection.
Solution design.
Multi-entity and multi-country requirements.
Finance and management reporting requirements.
Procurement and inventory workflows.
Approval workflows and controls.
User roles and permissions.
Data preparation and migration.
System integrations.
User Acceptance Testing (UAT).
Training and implementation readiness.
Cutover and go-live.
Post-implementation stabilisation and optimisation.
The role must have sufficient technical and functional expertise to independently assess and challenge recommendations made by vendors and implementation partners.

E. Systems Integration & Automation

Design an integrated technology environment across the Group.
Define integration requirements and data flows between core systems.
Ensure appropriate use of APIs, middleware and other integration technologies.
Establish systems of record and minimise unnecessary duplication of data.
Identify and implement workflow and process automation opportunities.
Ensure systems provide a consistent flow of information across relevant functions.
The technology landscape may include:

ERP and Finance
CRM
Contact Centre and omnichannel communications
Booking and POS
HR and workforce management
Inventory and procurement
E-commerce
Marketing technology
Business intelligence and reporting
AI and workflow automation
F. Data Architecture, Migration & Governance

Develop the Group's data architecture and governance framework.
Identify master data and establish clear data ownership.
Assess the quality and integrity of existing data.
Lead data cleansing, mapping, migration, reconciliation and validation.
Establish system-of-record ownership for critical data.
Implement appropriate controls over data access, quality and integrity.
Ensure technology architecture supports accurate Group-wide reporting.
Prepare the Group's data environment for future analytics, automation and AI capabilities.
G. Vendor & Implementation Partner Management

Lead the evaluation and selection of technology vendors and implementation partners.
Develop structured RFP/RFQ processes where appropriate.
Evaluate proposals, demonstrations, architecture and implementation methodologies.
Assess total cost of ownership and long-term commercial implications.
Support contract and commercial negotiations.
Define clear scopes, deliverables, milestones and acceptance criteria.
Challenge vendor recommendations where appropriate.
Monitor delivery against agreed scope, budget and timelines.
Manage change requests and scope control.
Hold vendors accountable for delivery and resolution of implementation issues.
The Group Technology Transformation Lead will represent the Group's interests and requirements, ensuring ownership of technology strategy remains internally with the business.

H. Programme & Project Governance

Establish appropriate governance for the overall technology transformation programme.
Develop project plans, workstreams, milestones and dependencies.
Define business owners, system owners and project responsibilities.
Maintain project budgets, risk registers, decision logs and issue trackers.
Establish change-control processes.
Define testing and implementation-readiness requirements.
Establish clear go-live criteria.
Identify and escalate risks appropriately.
Provide concise, decision-focused progress reporting to the CEO and management team.
I. Change Management & User Adoption

Assess the organisational impact of technology changes.
Partner with HR and department heads to develop appropriate change-management plans.
Identify key users and system champions.
Coordinate user training and readiness.
Ensure SOPs and workflows are updated to reflect new systems and processes.
Monitor system adoption and identify capability or training gaps.
Address operational issues following implementation.
Ensure new systems replace legacy processes and unnecessary manual work rather than creating additional layers of administration.
J. Technology Governance & Continuous Improvement

Establish sustainable Group technology governance.
Define system, business, vendor and data ownership.
Establish user-access and change-management controls.
Maintain appropriate system and technical documentation.
Review licence and subscription utilisation.
Establish regular system and vendor performance reviews.
Support business continuity and technology risk management.
Continuously evaluate opportunities to improve the Group's technology environment after implementation.
3. Candidate RequirementsEssential Experience

Significant senior-level experience in technology transformation, enterprise systems, ERP implementation or a related field.
Demonstrable experience personally leading at least one significant Tier 1 ERP implementation within the last five years.
Proven end-to-end implementation experience covering requirements gathering, solution design, data migration, integrations, UAT, cutover, go-live and stabilisation.
Strong experience in enterprise systems integration and APIs.
Significant practical experience in data architecture, migration and governance.
Experience managing technology vendors and implementation partners.
Experience working across multiple business functions and legal entities.
Experience operating within multi-country or international environments.
Strong programme and project governance experience.
Demonstrated ability to develop technology business cases and evaluate ROI.
Strong commercial and operational understanding.
Experience working directly with senior executives and management teams.
Preferred Experience

Recent hands-on NetSuite implementation experience and/or relevant NetSuite certification.
Experience with CRM and customer-data platforms.
Contact centre and omnichannel technology.
Booking and POS systems.
HRIS and workforce-management platforms.
Inventory and procurement systems.
E-commerce platforms.
Business intelligence and analytics.
AI and workflow automation.
Multi-site customer-facing businesses such as beauty/wellness, healthcare, clinics, retail, hospitality or consumer services.
UAE and KSA operating experience.
4. Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Technology, Engineering or a related discipline.
Relevant postgraduate qualification is advantageous.
ERP, NetSuite, enterprise architecture, programme/project management or technology transformation certifications are advantageous.
Equivalent substantial professional experience may be considered.
5. Technical Competencies

The successful candidate should demonstrate strong working knowledge of:

Enterprise architecture and ERP systems.
Systems integration and APIs.
Data architecture and migration.
Master-data management.
CRM and customer journeys.
Finance and accounting workflows.
HR systems.
Contact-centre technology.
Booking and POS systems.
Inventory and procurement.
E-commerce.
Business intelligence and reporting.
Workflow automation and AI.
Technology governance and access controls.
Vendor and implementation-partner management.
The role does not require the individual to be a software developer; however, they must have sufficient technical depth to independently evaluate architecture, challenge technical recommendations and make informed technology decisions.

6. Leadership & Behavioural CompetenciesBusiness Partner

Understands the commercial and operational requirements of the organisation and translates them into effective technology decisions.

Commercially Minded

Evaluates technology based on business value, ROI, scalability and total cost of ownership rather than functionality alone.

Hands-On

Comfortable working directly with data, requirements, processes, systems and vendors rather than operating solely at strategic level.

Operationally Focused

Invests time in understanding how departments and locations actually operate before recommending solutions.

Technically Credible

Able to challenge vendors, implementation partners and technical consultants from an informed position.

Strategic & Pragmatic

Can design a long-term technology architecture while recognising the Group's immediate operational and commercial requirements.

Accountable

Takes end-to-end ownership of outcomes from initial strategy through implementation and stabilisation.

Strong Communicator

Able to communicate complex technology matters clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Collaborative

Builds effective working relationships across countries, businesses and functions while maintaining clear accountability.

7. Key Performance Indicators

Performance will be measured against agreed annual objectives, which may include:

Delivery of an approved Group technology strategy and roadmap.
Achievement of agreed transformation milestones.
Delivery of projects within approved budgets and timelines.
Successful ERP implementation and stabilisation.
Accuracy and completeness of migrated data.
Successful integration of core business systems.
Reduction in manual processes and system duplication.
Improvement in management reporting and data visibility.
System adoption and user readiness.
System reliability and operational stability.
Vendor performance and cost management.
Measurable operational and commercial benefits from technology investments.
Scalability of the technology environment to support Group expansion.
8. Initial Priorities – First 6 Months

The initial mandate will be to establish control, clarity and direction across the Group's technology environment.

Key priorities will include:

Understand each business's strategy, commercial model and operational processes.
Complete an audit of current systems, vendors, contracts, integrations and technology expenditure.
Identify immediate technology risks, gaps and opportunities.
Establish system ownership and technology governance.
Support management with immediate technology and vendor decisions.
Complete structured requirements gathering across key functions.
Define the proposed future-state technology architecture.
Evaluate major platform options, including NetSuite where appropriate.
Develop a prioritised implementation roadmap, budget and business case.
Present recommendations and implementation priorities to the CEO and management team.
9. Long-Term Mandate

Over the following 2–3 years, the Group Technology Transformation Lead will be accountable for delivering and embedding the Group's future technology environment.

This includes implementing the approved ERP and supporting platforms, integrating core systems, establishing reliable Group-wide data, improving automation and reporting, reducing manual processes and ensuring the architecture can support future businesses, locations and countries.

The role remains accountable beyond technical implementation. Success requires ensuring that systems are adopted, operationally stable and delivering measurable commercial and operational value.
